picks.title: AI May Help Detect Rare Sperm in Men With Azoospermia
picks.excerpt: An AI system that scans testicular tissue samples for rare sperm in men with azoospermia was presented at ASRM 2026; researchers said it has already resulted in three live births.
picks.rationale: A clinical result tied to real patient outcomes: AI that finds rare sperm in testicular tissue from men with azoospermia has already led to three live births (ASRM 2026). Nothing in the 30-day history covers fertility or andrology.

picks.title: ChatGPT-5 misses half of distal radius fractures on x-rays
picks.excerpt: Rambam Health Care Campus researchers (Emergency Radiology, Oct 26) found ChatGPT-5 had 51.2% sensitivity and 61.6% accuracy on 370 wrist x-rays, missing 83 of 170 distal radius fractures.
picks.rationale: A patient-safety warning that clinicians can act on: a general-purpose chatbot missed 83 of 170 wrist fractures (51.2% sensitivity). The 10-10 GPT-5 card was a multimodal diagnosis benchmark, and the 10-16 card was about detecting AI-generated chest x-rays. Neither is this study.

picks.title: SIIM-CAIMI: AI triaging for ICH leads to faster turnaround times
picks.excerpt: A multisite University of Washington study of an AI intracranial hemorrhage triage system found 79.3% sensitivity and 94.2% specificity; median report turnaround for ICH-positive head CTs fell from 214 to 201 minutes and AI-flagged patients reached admission sooner.
picks.rationale: Real-world deployment evidence from a multisite University of Washington study: AI triage for brain bleeds (ICH) shortened report turnaround, and flagged patients were admitted sooner. The history has no ICH-triage card. The 10-22 PE-detection card covered a different finding and different sites. This is the second AuntMinnie card, which is the outlet cap.

picks.title: Scalable drift monitoring in medical imaging AI
picks.excerpt: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical medical imaging has advanced diagnostics but also poses challenges in maintaining long-term reliability as input data change. To address this, we present MMC+, a modular framework for scalable drift monitoring that builds on our CheXstray
picks.rationale: Post-deployment safety for clinical imaging AI: MMC+ monitors deployed models for input drift, which is the operational gap that regulators and the AMA have been raising. The 10-25 card on AI checking breast-cancer models audited trustworthiness of the models themselves. This one is about monitoring live input data, so it is distinct.

picks.title: UnitedHealthcare expands AI companion Avery to 21M members
picks.excerpt: UnitedHealthcare is expanding Avery, its generative AI companion for care coordination, to 21 million members.
picks.rationale: A patient-facing rollout: the largest U.S. insurer is putting a generative AI care-coordination companion in front of 21 million members. No UnitedHealthcare or Avery card exists in the history. The nearest payer or care-ops card is the 10-23 Sentara/Regard case-management tool, which is a different company and product.
